t:
That section 3(g) of the Railroad Retirement Act of 1974 is amended by inserting “(1)” after “(g)” and by inserting at the end thereof the following new subdivision:


“(2) 
Those portions of the annuity of an individual as are computed under subsections (b) and (d) of this section shall, if such individual’s annuity under section 2(a)(1) of this Act began to accrue on or before June 1, 1981, be increased by 32.5 per centum of the percentage increase, if any (rounded to the nearest one-tenth of 1 per centum), obtained by comparing the unadjusted Consumer Price Index for the calendar quarter ending March 31, 1981, with such index for the calendar quarter ending March 31, 1980. The unadjusted Consumer Price Index for any calendar quarter shall be the arithmetical mean of such index for the three months in such quarter. The increase provided under this subdivision shall be effective on June 1, 1981.”.

fable.w: This section only amends the Railroad Retirement Act to provide a formula-based cost-of-living increase to certain annuities effective June 1, 1981. There is no tempting participation language: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no outside party is brought into any federal decision. It is purely a benefit-computation provision.
fable.s: be increased by 32.5 per centum of the percentage increase, if any (rounded to the nearest one-tenth of 1 per centum), obtained by comparing the unadjusted Consumer Price Index

qwen_block.w: This section establishes a formula for calculating cost-of-living adjustments to railroad retirement annuities based on the Consumer Price Index. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. The calculation is automatic and statutory, requiring no input from the public, states, or other external entities.
qwen_block.s: Those portions of the annuity of an individual as are computed under subsections (b) and (d) of this section shall, if such individual’s annuity under section 2(a)(1) of this Act began to accrue on or before June 1, 1981, be increased by 32.5 per centum of the percentage increase, if any (rounded to the nearest one-tenth of 1 per centum), obtained by comparing the unadjusted Consumer Price Index for the calendar quarter ending March 31, 1981, with such index for the calendar quarter ending March 31, 1980.

opus.w: This section changes the Railroad Retirement Act so that certain annuity portions rise by a fixed percentage of the change in the Consumer Price Index, starting June 1, 1981. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. Referring to the CPI is not participation: it is a mechanical calculation using federal data, and no outside party has a role in any federal decision.
opus.b: **Step 1: Analysis.** One could be tempted to read this as involving an outside process, because the increase depends on the Consumer Price Index, a measure published by an outside source. That reading fails. The CPI comes from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, a federal agency, and the provision just applies a fixed formula to that number. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, or allowed to comment or sue before a decision. The section only sets out how Railroad Retirement annuities are calculated.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a formula for increasing railroad retirement annuities based on the Consumer Price Index. It does not require the federal government to consult or coordinate with any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making the decision. The increase is automatic based on statistical data, not a participatory process. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Those portions of the annuity of an individual as are computed under subsections (b) and (d) of this section shall, if such individual’s annuity under section 2(a)(1) of this Act began to accrue on or before June 1, 1981, be increased by 32.5 per centum of the percentage increase, if any (rounded to the nearest one-tenth of 1 per centum), obtained by comparing the unadjusted Consumer Price Index for the calendar quarter ending March 31, 1981, with such index for the calendar quarter ending March 31, 1980.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the reference to the Consumer Price Index implies some form of public input or data collection from the public. However, the CPI is a statistical measure calculated by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, not a participatory process where the public consults with the government to make a decision. The section merely sets a formula for calculating benefit increases based on an existing economic indicator. There is no requirement for the government to consult with, coordinate with, or receive input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making the decision to increase the annuity. The decision is automatic based on the index values.
